Disaggregate count columns into inferred death records

Source: R/disaggregate.R
disaggregate_source.Rd

Disaggregate count columns into inferred death records

Usage

disaggregate_source(
  config_path,
  extracted_file = NULL,
  disaggregated_destination = paste0("{project_root}/disaggregated/{state}/",
    "{vintage}_{years}"),
  force = FALSE,
  source_table_id = NULL
)

Arguments

config_path

Source YAML path.

extracted_file

Optional extracted RDS path for legacy configs, or a directory of table-ID RDS files for inline tables.

disaggregated_destination

Directory template for inferred artifacts.

force

Rewrite even if a valid cache entry exists.

source_table_id

Optional table ID; by default process all tables.

Value

Results keyed by table ID, with paths, status, and record count.

Details

Run explicitly after extract_source() and before clean_source() for a table declaring top-level disaggregate. Simple counts use count_column and a table-specific expected_record_count. A pivot instead selects ordered pivot_columns, values_column_name (category), and count_column_name (intermediate count); count_column must equal that intermediate name. Consumed count columns are removed and other source text is carried forward. Do not select overlapping totals and subgroups: an expected count checks row count, not whether categories are disjoint.

Alternatively, a trusted script defines disaggregate_records(records, source_config) and returns source-shaped character rows with record_locator referencing an original extracted row. It may return zero or multiple rows per original. The engine groups rows by extracted order, retains script order within each group, and replaces those references with inferred locators. Formats may share a definition without an expected count; each inheriting table supplies its own count, replaces the entire definition, or opts out with disaggregate: null.

The suffix !Inferred N records generation order per original source row, not an agency-reported individual or durable person identity. Review corrections targeting these locators after source or script reordering. Zero counts yield no rows. An expected count mismatch or invalid count leaves any prior artifact pair unchanged. The sidecar records source_record_count and record_count (inferred rows). Cleaning preserves the inferred row count; post-clean filtering checks remaining rows.
